ports.name: i_tx_valid
ports.meaning: Transmit stream: i_tx_data holds a byte to send

ports.name: o_tx_ready
ports.meaning: Transmit stream: the transmitter can accept a byte at the next edge

ports.name: i_tx_data
ports.meaning: Transmit stream: byte to send; bit 0 is sent first

ports.name: o_rx_valid
ports.meaning: Receive stream: the holding register holds a byte

ports.name: i_rx_ready
ports.meaning: Receive stream: the consumer takes the held byte at this edge

ports.name: o_rx_data
ports.meaning: Receive stream: received byte; bit 0 was received first; qualified by o_rx_valid

ports.name: o_rx_frame_err
ports.meaning: Receive stream: 1 when the stop bit of the held byte was sampled as 0; qualified by o_rx_valid

ports.name: o_rx_overrun
ports.meaning: One-cycle pulse: a received byte was dropped because the holding register was full

ports.name: i_rxd
ports.meaning: Serial receive line, idle high, asynchronous to i_clk, synchronised inside the block

checks.title: Outputs change only at i_clk rising edges or reset assertion
checks.behavior: Any value change on o_txd, o_tx_ready, o_rx_valid, o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err or o_rx_overrun happens only in the simulation time step of a rising edge of i_clk or a falling edge of i_rst_n. Changes of i_tx_valid, i_tx_data and i_rx_ready (driven after the rising edge) and of i_rxd (driven at the falling edge) never cause an output change in their own time step.

checks.title: Output values while reset is asserted, including immediately after asynchronous assertion
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of i_clk at which i_rst_n=0, and also one simulation time step after every falling edge of i_rst_n (before any further i_clk edge): o_txd=1, o_tx_ready=1, o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=8'h00, o_rx_frame_err=0, o_rx_overrun=0.

checks.title: Delivery into an empty holding register at V=M+2
checks.behavior: Uses the RX reference model described in the assumptions, which gives T0, M=T0+H+9N, V=M+2, the byte (bit i = s(T0+H+(i+1)N)) and s(M). At delivery edge V with i_rst_n=1, if o_rx_valid=0 is sampled at V, then at V+1: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data equals the model byte, o_rx_frame_err = NOT s(M), and o_rx_overrun=0.

checks.title: Held byte taken at the delivery edge itself loads the new byte, no overrun
checks.behavior: At model delivery edge V with i_rst_n=1, if o_rx_valid=1 and i_rx_ready=1 are sampled at V, then at V+1: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data equals the new model byte, o_rx_frame_err = NOT s(M) of the new frame, and o_rx_overrun=0.

checks.title: Overrun drop at V keeps the held byte; one-cycle pulse
checks.behavior: At model delivery edge V with i_rst_n=1, if o_rx_valid=1 and i_rx_ready=0 are sampled at V, then at V+1: o_rx_overrun=1, o_rx_valid=1, and o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err equal their values sampled at V. At V+2 (if i_rst_n stayed 1): o_rx_overrun=0.

checks.title: o_rx_overrun only after a drop edge, independent of o_rx_valid
checks.behavior: At every rising edge E+1 where i_rst_n=1 at both E and E+1: o_rx_overrun=1 if and only if E is a model drop edge (a V with o_rx_valid=1 and i_rx_ready=0 sampled at V). Otherwise o_rx_overrun=0. This does not depend on o_rx_valid at E+1 or on i_rx_ready after V. Glitch detections (s(T0+H)=1) and frames cleared by reset never create a drop edge.

checks.title: Consumer take empties the holding register
checks.behavior: At a rising edge E that is not a model delivery edge, if i_rst_n=1, o_rx_valid=1 and i_rx_ready=1 are sampled, then at E+1: o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err are unchanged from E, and o_rx_overrun=0.

checks.title: Held byte is stable until taken
checks.behavior: At a rising edge E that is not a model delivery edge, if i_rst_n=1, o_rx_valid=1 and i_rx_ready=0 are sampled, then at E+1: o_rx_valid=1, and o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err equal their values at E.

checks.title: Empty register: i_rx_ready has no effect; data and flag keep the last loaded values
checks.behavior: At a rising edge E that is not a model delivery edge, if i_rst_n=1 and o_rx_valid=0 are sampled (any i_rx_ready), then at E+1: o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err are unchanged, and o_rx_overrun=0. In addition, between two consecutive samples with i_rst_n=1, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err change only if the earlier edge loaded a byte (CHK-003 or CHK-004).

checks.title: Transmit handshake, acceptance condition and idle values
checks.behavior: A TX reference model records an acceptance edge E0 if and only if i_tx_valid=1, o_tx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1 are all sampled at that rising edge. A frame is active at samples E0+1 to E0+10N. The model is cleared when i_rst_n=0. (a) If i_tx_valid=1, o_tx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1 at edge E, then at E+1 o_tx_ready=0 and o_txd=0 (the start bit is in the first cycle after the handshake). (b) At every edge E with i_rst_n=1 where no frame is active, o_tx_ready=1 and o_txd=1. (c) An edge where i_tx_valid=0 or o_tx_ready=0 starts no frame. Any o_txd or o_tx_ready value that differs from the active-frame values (CHK-011, CHK-012) or the idle values in (b) is a failure.

checks.title: Cycle-exact transmit frame content (8N1, LSB first, N cycles per bit)
checks.behavior: For each acceptance edge E0 (from CHK-010), let D be the value of i_tx_data sampled at E0. For every k from 0 to 10N-1, o_txd sampled at edge E0+k+1 equals frame bit j=floor(k/PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT), where bit 0=0, bit j=D[j-1] for j=1..8, and bit 9=1. This holds as long as i_rst_n stays 1. Values of i_tx_data at all other edges do not affect o_txd.

checks.title: o_tx_ready timing during a frame
checks.behavior: For each acceptance edge E0 (with i_rst_n=1 throughout): o_tx_ready=0 at every sample from E0+1 to E0+10N-1 inclusive (10N-1 cycles), and o_tx_ready=1 at E0+10N.

checks.title: No idle cycle between back-to-back frames; idle high after a frame
checks.behavior: For acceptance edge E0: (a) If E0+10N is also an acceptance edge, o_txd=1 at E0+10N (stop bit) and o_txd=0 at E0+10N+1, with no idle sample in between. (b) If E0+10N is not an acceptance edge, o_txd=1 at every sample from E0+10N+1 up to and including the next acceptance edge E1, and o_txd=0 at E1+1.

checks.title: CFG-MIN: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=4
checks.behavior: With the smallest legal bit period, framing, timing, sampling points and glitch rejection still hold, with minimum sampling margins.
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=4 (H=2). Run the tests of CHK-030 (20 bytes), CHK-023 (patterns A and B), CHK-024 (L=1,2,3), CHK-025(a) and CHK-026(a,b), with all assertions active.
checks.expected: Transmit frames are 40 cycles long. o_tx_ready=0 for samples E0+1 to E0+39 and 1 at E0+40. Receive sample edges are S_i=T0+2+4(i+1) and M=T0+38. Delivery is at V=T0+40, so o_rx_valid is sampled 1 at T0+41. Glitches of 1 or 2 samples are rejected and 3 samples are accepted. Overrun and take-at-V behave as in CHK-026.

checks.title: CFG-ODD: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=5 (H=floor(N/2)=2)
checks.behavior: With an odd N the sampling offset is H=floor(N/2)=2, with samples every N edges after that, and transmit bits are N cycles long.
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=5. Run CHK-030 (20 bytes), CHK-023 (patterns A and B), CHK-024 (L=1,2,3) and CHK-025(a).
checks.expected: Transmit frames are 50 cycles. o_tx_ready=0 for samples E0+1 to E0+49 and 1 at E0+50. Each transmit bit is 5 samples long. Receive samples are at T0+2+5(i+1), M=T0+47 and V=T0+49 (o_rx_valid sampled 1 at T0+50). Glitches of 1 or 2 samples are rejected and 3 are accepted. Pattern A gives D and pattern B gives ~D with o_rx_frame_err=1.

checks.title: CFG-WIDE: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=1024
checks.behavior: With a wide N, the counters reach the full bit period and the half-bit offset without wrapping.
checks.stimulus: PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=1024 (H=512). Transmit 2 back-to-back bytes (8'hA5, 8'h5A). Receive one pattern-A sampling-point frame (8'h96), a glitch of 512 samples, and a 513-sample low pulse followed by high. Then run a loopback of one byte.
checks.expected: Transmit: o_tx_ready=0 for samples E0+1 to E0+10239 and 1 at E0+10240. Each bit is 1024 samples. The second start bit appears at E0+10241. Receive: samples at T0+512+1024(i+1), M=T0+9728, V=T0+9730, and 8'h96 is delivered with o_rx_frame_err=0. The 512-sample glitch produces nothing. The 513-sample pulse gives 8'hFF at its V. Loopback: delivered at E0+H+9N+3=E0+9731.

checks.title: Full duplex: simultaneous and independent transmit and receive
checks.behavior: Transmit handshakes and frames run at the same time as receive deliveries, takes and overruns, and neither changes the timing or outputs of the other.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Hold i_tx_valid=1 with 40 random bytes, back to back. At the same time, send 40 receive frames with random gaps of 0 to N and random i_rx_ready. Align the stimulus so that some receive delivery edges V and some take edges fall exactly on transmit acceptance edges.
checks.expected: Transmit acceptances happen exactly every 160 edges and o_txd matches CHK-011 and CHK-013. Every receive delivery, take and overrun matches the RX model (CHK-003 to CHK-009) at the same cycles the model predicts without transmit activity. No assertion fails at edges where both happen.

checks.title: Loopback o_txd to i_rxd through a half-cycle delay
checks.behavior: Bytes sent from the transmitter and looped back through a half-cycle delay are received intact with a fixed latency.
checks.stimulus: N=16. i_rxd copies o_txd at every falling edge of i_clk (a half-cycle delay). i_rx_ready=1. Hold i_tx_valid=1 with bytes 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and 28 random bytes.
checks.expected: For each acceptance edge E0: T0=E0+1, M=E0+1+H+9N, V=E0+H+9N+3=E0+155, and o_rx_valid is sampled 1 at E0+156. o_rx_data equals the byte sent, o_rx_frame_err=0, and o_rx_overrun stays 0. All 32 bytes are received in order.

checks.title: Asynchronous reset mid transmit frame, mid receive frame and while a byte is held
checks.behavior: Reset asserted between clock edges takes effect at once. A frame being sent is abandoned and the rest of it is never sent. A frame being received is discarded. A held byte is discarded.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Each sub-case drives i_rst_n low 30% of a clock period after a rising edge, holds it low for 3 cycles, then releases it synchronously. (a) Accept i_tx_data=8'h00 at E0. Assert reset when o_txd=0, about 4N+3 cycles after E0. Release with i_tx_valid=0 and keep it at 0 for 12N cycles. (b) Drive receive frame 8'h00 on i_rxd. Assert reset at about T0+H+4N. Hold i_rxd=1 from assertion until 12N cycles after release. (c) Load byte 8'h81 with its stop bit sampled 0, so o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'h81 and o_rx_frame_err=1, with i_rx_ready=0. Assert reset. After release keep i_rx_ready=0 and send a normal frame 8'h42.
checks.expected: In every sub-case, one time step after i_rst_n falls and before the next rising edge: o_txd=1, o_tx_ready=1, o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_data=8'h00, o_rx_frame_err=0 and o_rx_overrun=0. (a) After release, o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1 at every sample for at least 10N samples, so no part of the abandoned frame appears. (b) After release, o_rx_valid=0, o_rx_overrun=0 and o_rx_frame_err=0 for at least 10N+H+4 samples, which goes past the original delivery edge. (c) o_rx_valid stays 0 after release. Frame 8'h42 is delivered at V=T0+H+9N+2: o_rx_valid goes 0->1 when sampled at V+1, o_rx_data=8'h42, o_rx_frame_err=0, and o_rx_overrun stays 0 (no overrun, because the held byte was discarded).

checks.title: No activity during reset; idle transmitter and receiver after release
checks.behavior: During reset no transmit byte is accepted and no start bit is detected. After release the transmitter accepts a byte at the first edge R1, and the receiver is idle and receives normally.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (A) Hold i_rst_n=0 for 6 cycles. During that time drive i_tx_valid=1 with i_tx_data=8'hA5, and toggle i_rxd 1,0,1,0 at falling edges, ending at 1 at least 2 cycles before release. Release i_rst_n synchronously and set i_tx_valid=0 in the same step, so it is 0 at R1. Keep i_rxd=1. Wait 12N cycles. (B) Reset again for 3 cycles. Release with i_tx_valid=1 and i_tx_data=8'h3C, and drop i_tx_valid after the handshake. Three cycles after release, start receive frame 8'h96 on i_rxd with i_rx_ready=1.
checks.expected: (A) o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1 at every sample during reset and for 10N+2 samples after release. o_rx_valid=0 and o_rx_overrun=0 throughout. (B) The handshake happens at R1, the first rising edge with i_rst_n=1. Sampled at R1+1: o_tx_ready=0 and o_txd=0. The frame for 8'h3C follows CHK-011. Frame 8'h96 is delivered at V=T0+H+9N+2 (T0+154) with o_rx_data=8'h96 and o_rx_frame_err=0.

checks.title: Line low at reset release is detected as a start bit
checks.behavior: The synchronizer resets to 1, so s(R1-1)=1. A line that is 0 at R1 makes R1 the start edge T0. If the line stays low, exactly one byte 8'h00 with o_rx_frame_err=1 is produced.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Hold i_rxd=0 during reset (at least 3 cycles) and through the release. Keep i_rxd=0 for 40N cycles after R1. Set i_rx_ready=0 until o_rx_valid=1, then set it to 1. Then drive i_rxd=1 for N cycles and send frame 8'hA5.
checks.expected: T0=R1. o_rx_valid is first sampled 1 at R1+H+9N+3 (delivery edge V=R1+H+9N+2=R1+154) with o_rx_data=8'h00 and o_rx_frame_err=1. After the byte is taken, o_rx_valid stays 0 and o_rx_overrun stays 0 for the rest of the low period, so there is no second frame. Frame 8'hA5 is then delivered at its V with o_rx_frame_err=0.

checks.title: Basic receive of directed and random bytes with exact latency
checks.behavior: Correct 8N1 frames on i_rxd, LSB first, are confirmed at T0+H and delivered at V=T0+H+9N+2. The 2-edge synchronizer latency is visible at the ports.
checks.stimulus: N=16 (H=8). i_rx_ready held at 1. On i_rxd, changing only at falling edges of i_clk, send frames 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA, 8'h01, 8'h80 and 20 random bytes. Each bit lasts exactly 16 cycles. Leave idle-high gaps of at least 2N between frames.
checks.expected: For each frame: o_rx_valid is sampled 1 at T0+155 (V=T0+154) and 0 at T0+156, because it is taken at V+1. o_rx_data equals the byte sent, with bit i taken from data-bit period i. o_rx_frame_err=0 and o_rx_overrun=0 throughout. There are 26 deliveries in order.

checks.title: Sampling-point test at the exact sampling edges
checks.behavior: Only s(T0-1), s(T0), s(T0+H), s(T0+H+(i+1)N) for i=0..7, and s(M) with M=T0+H+9N affect the frame. i_rxd at all other edges is ignored.
checks.stimulus: N=16 (H=8, sample edges S_i=T0+8+16(i+1), M=T0+152). i_rx_ready=1. Bytes are 8'h55, 8'hAA, 8'h0F, 8'hF0, 8'h00, 8'hFF and 10 random bytes. Pattern A: s(T0-1)=1, s(T0)=0, s(T0+H)=0, s(S_i)=D[i] and s(M)=1. At every other edge from T0+1 to M+1, drive the complement of the value at the nearest sample point, so the line is 1 at T0+1..T0+7, !D[i] at S_i-1 and S_i+1, and 0 at M-1 and M+1. Drive 1 from M+2. Pattern B: start bit 0 from T0 to T0+H. Data and stop bits are correct everywhere except at S_i and M, where they are inverted (s(S_i)=!D[i], s(M)=0). Leave at least 2N idle cycles between frames.
checks.expected: Pattern A: o_rx_data=D and o_rx_frame_err=0, delivered at V=T0+154. The 0 at M+1 is detected as a start and rejected as a glitch at M+1+H, so no extra byte or overrun follows. Pattern B: o_rx_data=~D and o_rx_frame_err=1 at V=T0+154. Exactly one delivery per frame.

checks.title: Start-bit glitch rejection and restart after a glitch
checks.behavior: Low pulses of 1 to H samples starting at T0 are rejected, with no byte, no flag and no pulse. A pulse of H+1 samples is accepted. A new start can be detected at any edge after T0+H, needing only one high sample before it.
checks.stimulus: N=16 (H=8). Run each case twice: (i) register empty with i_rx_ready=1; (ii) byte 8'h5A held with i_rx_ready=0. (a) For L=1..8: i_rxd high for at least N cycles, low for exactly L samples (edges T0..T0+L-1), then high for at least 2N cycles. (b) L=9: low for edges T0..T0+8, then high. (c) Low for edges T0..T0+7, high only at edge T0+8, then from T0+9 a frame 8'h33 (start bit low for N cycles, data bits, stop bit).
checks.expected: (a) For every L from 1 to 8, in both runs: o_rx_valid, o_rx_data and o_rx_frame_err do not change, and o_rx_overrun stays 0. (b) The start is confirmed. A byte 8'hFF with o_rx_frame_err=0 is delivered at V=T0+154 in run (i). In run (ii), o_rx_overrun=1 only at sample T0+155 and 8'h5A stays held. (c) The glitch is rejected at T0+8 and a new start is detected at T0'=T0+9. Run (i): 8'h33 is delivered at T0'+154. Run (ii): overrun pulse at T0'+155.

checks.title: Back-to-back receive frames and a new start at M+1
checks.behavior: The receiver accepts frames with no idle bit between them. It returns to idle after M and can detect a start at M+1. Bytes are delivered in the order their frames completed.
checks.stimulus: N=16. i_rx_ready=1. (a) Send 10 frames (8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and 6 random bytes) with each next start bit starting at once after the previous stop bit, every bit exactly 16 cycles, changes at falling edges. (b) A frame 8'hC3 whose stop bit is 1 only at sample M (0 from edge M+1), immediately followed by frame 8'h3C whose start bit begins at M+1.
checks.expected: (a) T0_k = T0_1 + 160(k-1), and each byte is delivered at V_k = T0_k+154 with the correct data, o_rx_frame_err=0, no overrun, in order. (b) 8'hC3 is delivered at M+2 with o_rx_frame_err=0. 8'h3C is detected at T0'=M+1 and delivered at M+1+154.

checks.title: i_rx_ready held at 0, held at 1, random, and take at V
checks.behavior: A low i_rx_ready never stalls the receiver. A full register at V with i_rx_ready=0 causes an overrun. A take at V itself loads the new byte with no overrun.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (a) i_rx_ready=0, then 4 back-to-back frames B1..B4, then i_rx_ready=1 for one cycle. (b) Hold B1 with i_rx_ready=0, send B2, and set i_rx_ready=1 only at the edge V2. (c) Hold B1, send B2, and set i_rx_ready=1 only at the edge V2-1. (d) i_rx_ready held at 1 for 10 frames. (e) i_rx_ready random (50%) for 60 frames with random gaps of 0 to 3N.
checks.expected: (a) B1 is loaded at V1. At V2, V3 and V4 (each at T0_k+154): o_rx_overrun=1 at Vk+1 and 0 at Vk+2, with o_rx_data=B1 unchanged. After the take, o_rx_valid=0. (b) At V2+1: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=B2, o_rx_overrun=0. (c) o_rx_valid=0 at V2, then 1 with B2 at V2+1, and no overrun. (d) No overrun and every byte delivered. (e) All rx assertions (CHK-003 to CHK-009) pass, and deliveries plus overrun pulses equal the number of confirmed frames.

checks.title: Frame error with an empty register and with the byte dropped by overrun
checks.behavior: A frame with s(M)=0 completes at M. It is delivered with o_rx_frame_err=1 and its sampled data bits. If it is dropped by overrun, its flag is not reported.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (a) Register empty, i_rx_ready=0. Send 8'hC3 with the stop bit held at 0 for N cycles, then the line high for 2N. Then set i_rx_ready=1 for one cycle. Then send normal frame 8'h3C. (b) Hold 8'h11 (o_rx_frame_err=0) with i_rx_ready=0. Send 8'hEE with the stop bit at 0, then the line high. Then take 8'h11.
checks.expected: (a) At V=T0+154: o_rx_valid=1, o_rx_data=8'hC3, o_rx_frame_err=1. These are held until the take, then o_rx_valid=0 while o_rx_frame_err stays 1. 8'h3C is then delivered with o_rx_frame_err=0. (b) o_rx_overrun=1 only at V+1. o_rx_data=8'h11 and o_rx_frame_err=0 stay unchanged. After the take, o_rx_valid=0 and 8'hEE is never delivered.

checks.title: Idle line and break condition
checks.behavior: A line held at 1 delivers nothing. A line held at 0 gives exactly one frame (8'h00 with o_rx_frame_err=1, or an overrun drop). No further frame starts until the line has been sampled as 1 and then as 0.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (a) i_rxd=1 for 30N cycles with i_rx_ready random. (b) Register empty, i_rx_ready=1. i_rxd falls at T0 and stays 0 for 50N cycles. Then it is 1 for exactly one sample X, then a frame 8'h5A starts at X+1. (c) Hold 8'h77 with i_rx_ready=0, then the same break of 50N cycles.
checks.expected: (a) o_rx_valid=0 and o_rx_overrun=0 at every sample. (b) Exactly one delivery: 8'h00 with o_rx_frame_err=1 at V=T0+154. No further o_rx_valid rise or overrun while the line is low. 8'h5A is detected at X+1 and delivered at X+1+154. (c) Exactly one o_rx_overrun pulse, at T0+155. 8'h77 with o_rx_frame_err=0 stays held, and there are no more pulses during the break.

checks.title: Random receive regression against the reference model
checks.behavior: The reference model computes s(E) from i_rxd and applies the start, glitch, sampling, delivery, take and overrun rules exactly. The DUT matches it cycle by cycle.
checks.stimulus: N=16. 300 frames with random bytes, random gaps of 0 to 3N (including 0 for back-to-back), 10% with the stop bit at 0, 10% preceded by a glitch of random length 1..H, and random i_rx_ready. i_rxd changes only at falling edges.
checks.expected: CHK-003 to CHK-009 pass at every cycle. The sequence of delivered (o_rx_data, o_rx_frame_err) pairs equals the model's sequence of loaded frames in completion order. The count of overrun pulses equals the model's count of drops.

checks.title: Back-to-back transmit with i_tx_valid held at 1
checks.behavior: With i_tx_valid held at 1, one byte is accepted every 10N cycles. Frames follow each other with no idle cycle and in the order they were accepted.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Hold i_tx_valid=1 continuously. Present the bytes 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA, then 20 random bytes on i_tx_data. Change to the next byte synchronously after each edge where o_tx_ready=1 and i_tx_valid=1 were sampled. Decode o_txd with a monitor.
checks.expected: Acceptance edges are E0, E0+160, E0+320, ... (every 10N=160 edges), 24 in total. o_txd matches CHK-011 for each byte with no idle sample between frames. The decoded sequence is 8'h00, 8'hFF, 8'h55, 8'hAA and then the random bytes, in order. The whole stream lasts 24*160 cycles.

checks.title: Transmit with idle gaps and i_tx_data changing outside the handshake
checks.behavior: Only i_tx_data at the accepting edge is sent. Changes on i_tx_data at other edges have no effect.
checks.stimulus: N=16. Send 50 bytes. Before each one, wait a random idle gap of 0 to 3N cycles (including 0 and 1). Drive i_tx_valid=1 for exactly the handshake cycle. Drive a new random value on i_tx_data on every cycle, including while o_tx_ready=0 and while idle.
checks.expected: Each frame on o_txd carries exactly the i_tx_data value sampled at its acceptance edge (CHK-011). o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1 throughout every idle gap. There are 50 frames in total.

checks.title: i_tx_valid dropping before a handshake, back-pressure, no extra buffer
checks.behavior: Offers made while o_tx_ready=0 are neither accepted nor recorded. An offer withdrawn before a handshake sends nothing. An offer held until o_tx_ready=1 is accepted at E0+10N and sent exactly once.
checks.stimulus: N=16. (a) Accept 8'h12 at E0. Drive i_tx_valid=1 with i_tx_data=8'hED for cycles E0+1 to E0+100, then 0 from E0+101 onward. (b) Accept 8'h34 at E0. Hold i_tx_valid=1 with i_tx_data=8'hCB from E0+1 until the handshake, then drop it. (c) Single-cycle i_tx_valid pulse while o_tx_ready=1.
checks.expected: (a) Only 8'h12 is sent. From E0+161 onward, o_txd=1 and o_tx_ready=1 for at least 20N samples; 8'hED is never sent. (b) The handshake for 8'hCB happens exactly at E0+160. o_txd=0 at E0+161, and 8'hCB is sent once and then the line is idle. (c) The one-cycle pulse is accepted and its byte is sent.

Environment rule (ENV-002). Applied as a stimulus constraint: every simulation starts with i_rst_n=0 for at least 2 i_clk cycles.
Environment rule (ENV-003). Applied as a stimulus constraint: i_tx_valid, i_tx_data and i_rx_ready are driven just after rising edges with no X or Z.
Environment rule (ENV-004). Applied as a stimulus constraint: i_rxd changes only at falling edges of i_clk, including the loopback (designer decision).
Environment rule (ENV-004). Applied as a stimulus constraint: i_rxd is never X or Z after reset release.

assumptions: Timing notation: 'edge E' is a rising edge of i_clk. A value 'at E' is the value sampled just before edge E. 'Becomes X at edge E' or 'in the cycle after E' means the value is sampled as X at edge E+1.

s(E) is the value of i_rxd sampled at rising edge E. The testbench changes i_rxd only at falling edges, so s(E) is well defined. The 2-edge synchronizer latency is accounted for by the spec's V=M+2 (D-003).

RX reference model: R1 is the first rising edge with i_rst_n=1 after a release, and s(R1-1)=1. When idle, the start edge T0 is an edge with s(T0-1)=1 and s(T0)=0. At T0+H (H=floor(N/2)), s=1 means a glitch and a return to idle. Otherwise data bit i = s(T0+H+(i+1)N), M=T0+H+9N, the receiver is idle from M on (a start can be detected at M+1), and V=M+2 with load, take or drop as in Sections 7.6 to 7.8. Asserting i_rst_n clears all model state, including a frame that has passed M but whose V has not been reached yet.

TX reference model: E0 is an edge with i_tx_valid=1, o_tx_ready=1 and i_rst_n=1 sampled. D is i_tx_data sampled at E0. The frame occupies the samples at E0+1 to E0+10N. Asserting i_rst_n clears the model.

Section 8.5 (loopback latency) is not in the rule set. The expected loopback latency V=E0+H+9N+3 is derived from REQ-TX-010, REQ-RX-003 and D-003, using the half-cycle (falling-edge) loopback delay set by the designer decision.
Unless a test says otherwise, it runs with the default PARA_UART_CLKS_PER_BIT=16 (H=8), and all assertion groups (reset, tx, rx, gen) are active in every test and configuration.

decisions.question: ENV-004 requires i_rxd to change away from rising clock edges. The loopback test (UL-12.3-03) connects o_txd to i_rxd, and o_txd changes synchronously with the clock. Is the loopback exempt from ENV-004, or is a delay or falling-edge offset required?
decisions.answer: Not exempt. In the loopback test o_txd reaches i_rxd through a half-cycle delay (i_rxd changes at the falling edge of i_clk), so ENV-004 holds; no other delay is required.

decisions.question: UL-12.2-02 asks for lint or structural review of the synchronizer. Who owns that check, and how does it fit the simulation verification flow?
decisions.answer: The synchronizer structure (two flip-flops in series on i_rxd, nothing else in between) is checked on the RTL at gate D2 (docs/RTL_RULES.md RR-33, with nnc rtl-check), not by simulation. Simulation checks only its port-visible effect (the receive latency of D-003).
